title: Add predictive concurrency allocator with SLO-gating for canary routing
author: Priya Raman
description: Motivation: Canary evaluations often surface regressions caused by unexpected concurrency pressure on GPUs and model KV caches. This PR introduces a predictive concurrency allocator that uses short-window time-series features and a lightweight online estimator to predict occupancy and limit per-model concurrency before tail latency exceeds SLO thresholds. It ties into the existing canary pipeline so canaries can gate rollouts automatically when predicted saturation is likely. Design summary: - Runtime component: a new allocator service that subscribes to per-model throughput/latency streams and predicts short-term concurrency headroom using exponential smoothing and a small linear regressor. The allocator returns a recommended concurrency cap and a confidence score. - Canary integration: canary scheduler consults the allocator before opening traffic; if predicted tail-latency exceeds configured SLO margin the canary is paused and a soft rollback signal emitted. - Fallbacks: when the allocator is unavailable, we fall back to the static concurrency profiles. - Observability: new metrics (allocator_predicted_headroom, allocator_confidence, allocator_trigger_reason) and SLI dashboards added. - Config: exposed as a tunable in perf-canary Helm values with per-tenant overrides and a dry-run mode. Testing and validation: - Unit tests for estimator logic and boundary cases. - Integration tests in the perf-canary harness that replay historical traces and validate that the allocator reduces tail latency violations by ~35% in our samples. - Canary simulation suite to stress different traffic shapes (bursts, long tails, cold-start). Rollout plan: - Start in dry-run for 48h on canaries only (no gating). - Enable SLO gating for canaries with conservative thresholds for 2 weeks. - Gradually enable for low-risk models before wide rollout. Related work: builds on ENG-2134 (previous canary instrumentation) and complements the existing adaptive probe scheduler.
